title: DataPolicy
description: What a principal sees inside a table they are allowed to reach: row filters, column masks, hidden columns (FR-4). Kept separate from the subscription decision because the two answer different questions and compose differently.

maskingFunction.description: Strictness order, used verbatim by the conflict resolver when two policies mask the same column: NULLIFY > CONSTANT > HASH > REGEX_REPLACE > PARTIAL > ROUNDING > plaintext (FR-5.1).

showLast.description: PARTIAL: number of trailing characters kept, e.g. 4 for a national ID, phone number or card number.

roundTo.description: ROUNDING: YEAR or MONTH for dates, or a numeric bucket size. Date of birth to year of birth, salary to a band.

saltRef.description: HASH: reference to a per-column salt held in the secret store. Per-column and not global, so hashes stay joinable within a column but cannot be correlated across columns.

userAttribute.description: ATTRIBUTE_COMPARE and IN_LIST: the user-side attribute the column is compared against, for example branch.

entitlementKey.description: ENTITLEMENT_JOIN: the key column in row_entitlement that the secure view joins on, for mappings too complex to express as a comparison.

rawPredicate.description: RAW_PREDICATE: escape hatch, dialect-checked and never interpolated with user input. Authoring it requires elevated rights because it bypasses the IR the other kinds are validated against.

columns.description: Which columns this rule covers, by any facet: name, pattern, classification, tag, glossary term, data type or custom property (FR-4.2). Selecting by facet is what makes a newly tagged PII column masked the moment a steward tags it, with no policy edit.

condition.description: Cell masking: mask only on rows where this expression holds, for example dept not equal to user.department (FR-4.3). SQL Server dynamic data masking cannot express this, so the capability matrix must warn before apply rather than drop it silently.

rowFilters.description: ANDed with every other policy row filter at every scope level. Strictest wins; nothing here can widen what another layer restricted.
